key_insight: A coupled thermo-metallurgical FEM can predict heat-affected zone extent, grain evolution, and hardness changes during submerged arc welding of ASTM A516 Gr.70 steel.
engineering_relevance: The model helps welding engineers estimate microstructural and mechanical outcomes from process conditions, supporting more reliable joint design and process optimization.
method: 3D Gaussian volumetric heat source in DEFORM-3D to model localized thermal input
Custom user subroutine couples thermal cycles with Fe-Fe3C phase transformations, grain refinement, and hardness evolution
Temperature-dependent material properties included to capture cooling-rate effects in hypoeutectoid steel
evidence_signal: Validation against metallography and microhardness for pass 2.1 showed good agreement: about 4% for HAZ extension, under 10% for grain size, and about 5% for hardness.
watch_item: The framework is calibrated for a specific multipass weld pass and does not yet include real-time data assimilation or online bidirectional process updates.
paper_title: Development of a numerical model for microstructural evolution during submerged ARC welding of ASTM A516 GR.70 steel
